column1: # Ogle, Jarrett, Lanz, Cluver, Alatalo, Appleton & Mazzarella 2019, ApJ Letters, 'A Break in Spiral Galaxy Scaling Relations at the Upper Limit of Galaxy Mass' (arXiv:1909.09080), Table 1 'Super Spiral Sample'.
# Transcribed 2026-09-28 from the arXiv LaTeX source (e-print 3,957,201 bytes, sha256 5b6aac753432dc34...), fetched with the owner's approval for
# campaign_fresh_gravity CFG40.  23 massive spirals, optical H-alpha long-slit rotation curves (3 with Palomar Hale/DBSP, 20 with SALT/RSS; 1 arcsec slit on the r-band major axis).
# vmax is the paper's 'maximum deprojected speed v_max ... at radius r measured from sampled H-alpha rotation curve' (NOT an outer/flat-part speed); dvmax is the standard deviation of the
# rotation-curve-minus-spline residuals at the sampled points (printed in parentheses in the paper).  No HI masses exist: Mgas is a Kennicutt-1998 Schmidt-law estimate from a WISE W3 SFR and D25.
# For 2MFGC 10372 the paper prints '<10.4' (logMgas) and '<1.16' (logSFR): the bound values are given here with ul=1 (AGN contamination of W2/W3 flux); all other rows ul=0.

# The paper's own notes attribute: z to SDSS DR13; Rd and i to Simard et al. 2011 SDSS bulge+exponential-disk fits; Mstars to WISE W1 luminosity with M/L_W1=0.6; SFR to WISE 12 micron (Cluver et al. 2017).
# Columns: name = 2MASX/SDSS designation as printed; alt_name = OGC / 2MFGC name or '-' (paper prints \nodata); z = SDSS redshift (dimensionless, as printed, 5 dp);
# D25_kpc = isophotal diameter at Sigma_r = 25.0 mag/arcsec^2 (kpc); Rd_kpc = exponential disk scale length (kpc); i_deg = inclination (deg);
# logMdark = log10 of NFW dark-halo mass inside radius r from the paper's rotation-curve fit (Msun); logMstars = log10 stellar mass (Msun); logMgas = log10 cold-gas mass (Msun);
# logSFR = log10 star formation rate (units not stated in the paper's table; Msun/yr by convention); ul = 1 if logMgas and logSFR are upper limits, else 0;
# vmax = maximum deprojected rotation speed (km/s); dvmax = its quoted 1-sigma (km/s); r_kpc = radius at which vmax is reached (kpc).
